To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have mapped a non-exhaustive set of putative ammonium and nitate transporter in maize and that these transporters are expressed in different tissues and organs of the plant.

we identified a set of genes that are expressed in all plant organs, that we found a set of genes expressed in roots that are regulated by nitrogen availability, and that we found a gene expressed in silks and husk leaves that is also regulated by nitrogen availability.

(i) we mapped 20 nitrogen transporter genes in maize, which were expressed in all organs tested; (ii) we showed that nitrogen transporters were regulated by nitrogen starvation and resupplied; (iii) we observed three main expression patterns of nitrogen transporters depending on nitrogen supply.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of nitrogen transport in the soil plant continuum and will help to improve nitrogen management in agriculture.
the expression of nitrogen transporter genes and how they respond to nitrogen availability in maize plants at vegetative and reproductive development.

the expression of nitrogen transporter genes at different stages of plant development and under nitrogen starvation and resupplied conditions, which will help to understand the nitrogen transport mechanisms in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nitrate transporters NRT2.2, NRT2.3, NRT2,6, NRT3.2 and NRT3.3 and the ammonium transporters AMT1.2, AMT1.3 and AMT2.2 are expressed in all the tested organs and are regulated by the availability or the absence of nitrogen.
the nitrate and ammonum transport pathways are complex and highly dependent on plant development and environmental factors.
the expression of the genes encoding for the transporters of nitrate and ammonia is not only regulated by nitrogen availability, but also by other factors such as plant organ and growth stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maize plants are able to adapt their nitrogen uptake and use to the environment and the developmental stage.
the nitrogen transporter gene expression patterns in maize are organ dependent and nitrogen supply dependent.
maize is able to adapt its nitrogen transport system depending on its developmental stage and nitrogen availability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

nitrogen transporters are expressed in all plant organs and that they respond to nitrogen supply, suggesting that the expression of nitrogen transporter genes could be used as a tool to assess the nutritional status of maize plants.

nitrogen transporters in plants are more complex than previously thought, and that they are expressed in all organs of the plant and regulated by the availability and the nature of the nitrogen source.
maize is a good candidate for further studies on the regulation of nitrogen transporter genes and their potential use in crop breeding.
